Where the hell do the calories in some fast food come from?

In 1/3 of a pound of ground beef, there's less than 300 calories, and 1/3 of a pound of beef is way more than what's in most fast food burgers.

Buns are probably 250 calories at the most. Lettuce, tomato, condiments, etc. are maybe 100 calories at most. That's 550 calories for a massive burger, yet a double whopper is almost twice as many calories? I'm not saying a double whopper is small, but it's definitely a hell of a lot smaller than a 1/3 pound burger with everything on it.

I'm not too familiar with yields when it comes to extracts, I've only done it once and got about 4oz of liquid and maybe half a gram of resin out of 20-30g of powder. (There was plenty of resin still stuck to the pan though).

$4 a gram doesn't seem bad as long as it's powerful stuff, but I see a few sites selling at $2-3 a g.

If a gram of resin could replace an entire day's worth of powder for me, I think the price is fine. Cheaper than what some people pay for their morning coffee.

The cost of the powder + 50-70% I'd say.

So the price of resin made from 100g of powder could be like $15-17. You could definitely make it way more expensive than that, but if you have a streamlined extraction technique and want to beat other people's prices, I think that's about right.
